segments.narration: The US Air Force hauled away hundreds of tonnes of soil. It happened in the Mapimi desert, Durango, Mexico, in July 1970.
An Athena test rocket, launched from Green River, Utah toward White Sands, went off course and came down in the wrong country.
It carried two small containers of radioactive cobalt-57. Locals hired to guard the wreckage watched soldiers dig for months. Then the stories started.
Compasses spinning. Radios dead. Mutant plants. Visitors landing here to meet aliens. The region got a name: the Zone of Silence.
Researchers who actually worked there found nothing. Andrea Kaus, who studied the reserve, said nobody but the guides had trouble with radios or compasses. The silence was marketing.

verdicts.claim: In July 1970 an Athena RTV test rocket launched from the Green River Launch Complex in Utah toward White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico went off course and fell in the Mapimi Desert region of Mexico.
verdicts.note: 96% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 1 number(s)

verdicts.claim: The rocket was carrying two small containers of radioactive cobalt-57, and a local resident hired to guard the crash debris during recovery helped spread rumours about the area.
verdicts.note: 95% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 1 number(s)

verdicts.claim: The resulting urban legend holds that radio signals and other communications cannot be received in the area, with claims of spinning compasses, magnetic anomalies, mutated flora and fauna and extraterrestrial visitations, and the area became known as the Zone of Silence.
verdicts.note: 68% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article

verdicts.claim: Andrea Kaus, who carried out doctoral research on the Mapimi Biosphere Reserve, reported that neither she nor anyone she spoke to apart from the local zoneros had any trouble with their radios or compasses, and the legends are used locally to promote tourism.
verdicts.note: Kaus's quoted finding and the tourism-promotion point are both in Wikipedia. 'The silence was marketing' is the narration's summary of that sourced conclusion.
